- M/T Differential Rotating Torque - Check Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC. 1. Turn the vehicle to the OFF (LOCK) mode. 2. Raise the vehicle on a lift. Make sure it is securely supported, and allow all four wheels to rotate freely. 3. Shift the transmission into neutral. 4. Measure the rotating torque with a beam-type torque wrench in the direction shown. Rotate the torque wrench more than two complete turns, and take the maximum reading. 5. Shift the transmission into low gear, and measure the rotating torque again. 6. Calculate the rotating torque. 7. Repeat steps 3 through 6 for the other wheel. 8. Replace the limited slip differential assembly if the rotating torque is lower than the service limit. Service Limit: 2.5 N.m (0.25 kgf.m, 1.8 lbf.ft)

text:
# Clutch System Description - Clutch Pedal Position Switch (M/T)

Clutch pedal position switch A is installed on the clutch pedal.

Clutch pedal position switch A is mostly used to start up the engine by turning the vehicle to the ON mode or to restart the engine when recovering from an engine stall. This system works when the clutch is disengaged.

A clutch pedal stroke sensor is installed on the clutch pedal. The clutch pedal stroke sensor detects the level of clutch pedal force and reduces the number of the clutch pedal position switches used in the system.

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.

The signals from the clutch pedal stroke sensor are sent to the VSA modulator-control unit. The VSA modulator-control unit communicates with the PCM via the CAN communication lines.

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.

title: Manual Transmission System Description (Except K20C1 (M/T))
text:
# Manual Transmission System Description (Except K20C1 (M/T))

Reverse Lockout System

At vehicle speeds of 12 mph (20 km/h) or more, the PCM, which monitors the signals from the output shaft (countershaft) speed sensor, activates the reverse lockout solenoid, which pushes the select lock cam into the locked position. As a result, the select lever cannot rotate to the reverse select position, making it impossible to engage the reverse gear. As the vehicle speed drops to 9 mph (15 km/h) or less, the PCM turns off the reverse lockout solenoid. The select lock return spring pulls back the select lock cam, enabling the select lever to move freely so the reverse gear can be selected.

Vehicle speed | Inhibitor | Reverse selection

Above 12 mph (20 km/h) | ON | Not allowed

Below 9 mph (15 km/h) | OFF | Allowed

Vehicle OFF (LOCK) mode | OFF | Allowed

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.

General Operation

Improve operation feeling

The modified shift piece shape and clearance between pieces provide improved diagonal shift operation with reduced looseness.

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.

Reduction of double bump force

One-sided chamfering is applied to the synchro sleeve leading gear and gear dog, providing reduced "double-bump" load.

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.

MBS (Mainshaft Brake System) Mechanism

When the shift lever is moved to reverse, the 3rd-gear synchro is activated to brake the mainshaft, providing reduce reverse operation load.

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.

Constant mesh reverse gear mechanism

The constantly meshed helical gears provide reduced gear noise.

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC.

text:
# Clutch Hydraulic System Bleeding (M/T): Bleeding

NOTE:

- Do not reuse the drained fluid. Always use Honda DOT 3 Brake Fluid from an unopened container. Using a non-Honda brake fluid can cause corrosion and shorten the life of the system.

- Make sure no dirt or other foreign matter is allowed to contaminate the brake fluid.

- Do not spill brake fluid on the vehicle; it may damage the paint or plastic. If brake fluid gets on the paint or plastic, wash it off immediately with water.

- It may be necessary to limit the movement of the release fork with a block of wood to remove all the air from the system.

- Use fender covers to avoid damaging painted surfaces.

- Clutch Reservoir - Level Check Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC. 1. Make sure the brake fluid level in the clutch reservoir (A) is at the MAX (upper) level line (B).

Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC. | 1. Make sure the brake fluid level in the clutch reservoir (A) is at the MAX (upper) level line (B).

- Clutch Hydraulic System - Bleed Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC. 1. Attach one end of a clear tube to the bleeder screw (A), and put the other end into a container. 2. Loosen the bleeder screw to allow air to escape from the system. 3. Make sure there is an adequate supply of fluid in the reservoir, then slowly push the clutch pedal all the way down. Before releasing the pedal, have an assistant temporarily tighten the bleeder screw. Loosen the bleeder screw and push the clutch pedal down again. Repeat this step until no more bubbles appear from the clear tube. NOTE: Make sure the fluid level on the reservoir does not go below MIN (lower). 4. Tighten the bleeder screw securely. 5. Refill the brake fluid in the reservoir to the MAX (upper) level line. 6. Check the clutch operation, and check for leaks.

text:
# Synchro Sleeve and Hub Disassembly, Reassembly, and Inspection (M/T): Inspection

- Synchro Sleeve and Hub - Inspect Courtesy of HONDA, U.S.A., INC. 1. Inspect the gear teeth on all synchro hubs and synchro sleeves for wear (rounded off corners). 2. Install each synchro hub (A) in its mating synchro sleeve (B), and check for free movement. Make sure to match the three sets of longer teeth (C) (120 degrees apart) on the synchro sleeve with the three sets of deeper grooves (D) in the synchro hub. NOTE: Do not install the synchro sleeve with its longer teeth in the synchro hub slots (E) because it will damage the spring ring. If replacement is required, always replace the synchro sleeve and the synchro hub as a set.

NOTE:

- Where icon is shown, for further information see below.

- Prior to reassembling, clean all parts in solvent, dry them, and apply MTF to all contact surfaces and the O-rings.
